title: The universal closed-immersion locus for algebraic spaces is open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $A,C,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$, and $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Flatness, local finite presentation, local finite type, separatedness and universal closedness use the chartwise and topological definitions of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. A map is closed when its map of point spaces sends closed sets to closed sets. Assume that $p$ is locally of finite type and universally closed and that $q$ is separated. Then there is an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that, for every algebraic space $T$ over $S$ and every $h:T\to B$, the base change $f_T:A\times_BT\to C\times_BT$ is a closed immersion if and only if $h$ factors through $V$. A closed immersion of spaces means a representable morphism all of whose scheme base changes are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 05XA (spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-closed-immersion), all three hypotheses and arbitrary algebraic-space parameter changes.

proof.text: Put $P=A\times_B C$ and $\Gamma=(\mathrm{id}_A,f):A\to P$. The square with right side $\Delta_q:C\to C\times_B C$ and bottom map $(f\operatorname{pr}_A,\operatorname{pr}_C):P\to C\times_B C$ is cartesian: on every scheme test its pullback consists of triples $(a,c,y)$ with $f(a)=y=c$, hence is naturally $A$. Since $q$ is separated, $\Delta_q$ is a representable closed immersion. Thus $\Gamma$ is a closed immersion: each scheme test of its pullback is a scheme test of $\Delta_q$. By the closed-subspace properness statement, $\Gamma$ is proper, hence universally closed.

source.place: Tag 05XA proof, second sentence; graph factorization in spaces-morphisms Tag 04NX, proof of (1).

proof.text: Universal closedness is stable under base change directly from its definition: a further base change is a base change of the original map. It is stable under composition because, after any base change, the two induced point maps send closed sets successively to closed sets. The projection $P\to C$ is a base change of $p$, so $f=\operatorname{pr}_C\Gamma$ is universally closed. The projection $r:A\times_C A\to A$ is a base change of $f$; hence $p_2=p r$ is universally closed. In particular $p$ and $p_2$ are closed, by taking identity base changes.

source.place: Tag 05XA proof, verification of the hypotheses of 05X9; spaces-morphisms lemmas base-change-universally-closed and composition-universally-closed, expanded from the definition.

proof.text: Apply the unramified/injective parameter-locus statement to $(p,q,f)$. Its local-finite-type hypothesis is assumed for $p$; both closed-map hypotheses were proved in step 2. It gives an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ such that, for every algebraic-space map $h:T\to B$, $h$ factors through $V$ exactly when $f_T$ is unramified and universally injective.

Fix any such $T,h$. The map $f_T$ is universally closed by step 2, since it is the base change of $f$ along $C\times_B T\to C$. The closed-immersion criterion therefore identifies its being unramified and universally injective with its being a closed immersion. Combining this equivalence with step 3 gives the claimed universal property of $V$ for every algebraic-space parameter change.
